patches.diff: The Illinois Power of Attorney Act (755 ILCS 45) is not UPOAA. An agency lasts until death despite disability or appointment of a guardian (durable by default, as under UPOAA §104). Differences: the spouse-agent's authority ends on a judgment of dissolution or legal separation, not on filing as in UPOAA §110(b)(3); revocation may be in any manner communicated to the agent or a related person; the statutory short form needs one witness plus notary; guardians exercise agency powers only by court order under §2-10. Third parties who rely in good faith on a copy are protected and may demand an Agent's Certification and Acceptance of Authority (§2-8, amended by P.A. 104-609 eff. 1-1-27).

patches.diff: Illinois has no separate nondurable category. Every agency survives disability unless the instrument sets an earlier termination date or event (§§2-4(a), 2-5), so a nondurable power is just one that names incapacity as its end. This matches UPOAA §104's durable default.

UPOAA §109 also accepts a licensed psychologist and other persons the principal names.

patches.diff: Illinois uses Article IV of its Power of Attorney Act, not UHCDA. A health care agency may be revoked 'without regard to' the principal's mental or physical condition, with an optional 30-day delayed-revocation election. The agent's authority expressly outlasts death for anatomical gifts, autopsy, disposition of remains, record access and pending benefits claims, and those decisions override statutory priority lists. A dissolution judgment removes a spouse-agent. One qualified witness is required, and treating providers cannot serve as agent.

patches.diff: The Illinois Health Care Surrogate Act (755 ILCS 40) differs from UHCDA §5. Its fixed list includes adult grandchildren, a close friend by affidavit and the guardian of the estate; the provider must try to phone within 24 hours; forgoing life-sustaining treatment requires a certified 'qualifying condition'; surrogates other than guardians cannot consent to specific mental health services; and authority ends by statute on regained capacity, appointment of a guardian of the person, or death. No provision for an oral surrogate designation by the patient was found.

patches.diff: No Uniform Act baseline. The Illinois Disposition of Remains Act (755 ILCS 65) lets a person name a disposition agent in advance on a notarized statutory form that takes effect at death, but only after the agent signs an acceptance. A health care agent under an Article IV POA with disposition power also qualifies, and 755 ILCS 45/4-7(d) makes that agent's decision controlling. A military DD Form 93 designee overrides all others. A person charged with murder or voluntary manslaughter in the death loses the right. Courts must resolve disputes within 30 days. The Crematory Regulation Act section cited (410 ILCS 18/65) is scheduled for repeal 1-1-29 and has a pending amendment (P.A. 104-501).
